recorded: A bound agent receives no unrestricted or raw network egress; network is a typed capability the agent may request, Runtime decides, and the capability host enforces.
satisfied_when: Every harness firstmate can launch composes a session whose permission enforcement is active, AND the capability catalog's network.request row names an owner and a verifier. The probe below answers the first of those; the second is declared unobserved, so this entry cannot retire on the first alone.
unobserved_conditions: the capability catalog's network.request row names an owner and a verifier rather than carrying owner null and verifier null, which has no landed artifact to probe because that catalog exists as a proposal in data/cfvc-harness-and-capability/report.md section 6.3 rather than as tracked code
note: The ruling has two halves and only one of them has landed code to probe today. The probe answers the landed half: every worker launches with permission enforcement disabled, so the prohibition is recorded and not enforced. The other half is declared in unobserved_conditions rather than being probed or quietly dropped, because naming a not-yet-decided owner path would produce a probe that can never pass and dropping it would let this entry retire while network.request still carries owner null and verifier null - the verdict would then claim more than it observed. When that catalog lands as tracked code, this entry gains a second probe over it and the declaration goes away. Closing the gap is staged separately and this entry authorises none of it: retiring a bypass flag before bindings and adapters are proven would disarm every lane and enforce nothing.
